swap_risks: HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LMV358IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=RR vs TLV9002IDR: IN=RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 3000x (LMV358IDR: 15000 pA p.7 vs TLV9002IDR: 5 pA p.17); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: LMV358IDR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (5.5 V, p.5) than TLV9002IDR (7 V, p.14); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 5.5 V.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: LMV358IDR requires Vs,min >= 2.7 V (p.5) vs 1.8 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.
engineering_verdict: LMV358IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and TLV9002IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because rail-to-rail input/output swing differs; input bias current Ib differs 3000x (CMOS vs bipolar input stage); Vs,abs,max drops >=15% (5.5 V vs 7 V). Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 1 MHz (p.7) vs 1 MHz (p.17), supply ceiling 5.5 V (p.5) vs 5.5 V (p.14), Vos 7 mV (p.7) vs 1.6 mV (p.17), Ib 3000x gap (15000 vs 5 pA), voltage noise 39 vs 30 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LMV358IDR "5.5 V Absolute Maximum Ceiling — Destructive If Swapped into LM358 High-Voltage Boards" (p.5) and TLV9002IDR "5.5 V Max Supply Limit vs Pin-Identical High-Voltage SOIC-8 Op-Amps" (p.14). BOM decision: Choose LMV358IDR when matching your existing Texas Instruments SOIC-8 (D) qualification and -40..125 °C grade; choose TLV9002IDR when DC precision demands <= 1.6 mV max Vos or high-impedance sensors require pA-class input bias (5 pA). Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.8) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
